zh.question: 河水遇到石头会怎样？弯道的两边会发生一样的变化吗？
zh.observe: 先把石头放在中间，推进水流与泥沙；再选择靠左或拿走，比较路径。最后观察外侧冲刷和内侧沉积的标记。

academic.title: 河流沿势能降低的方向运动
academic.body: 河水的运动受重力、压力差和边界阻力共同影响。总体上水面沿河道降低，局部却可能有回流和涡旋。岩石、地形和河床材料会改变流路，但弯曲的河道并不一定由一块石头造成；岸边的微小差异、洪水与长期冲刷也能不断改变河道形状。画中的石头只是容易操纵的一个因素。

academic.title: 弯道把冲刷与沉积联系起来
academic.body: 许多冲积河流的弯道外岸更容易受到侵蚀，内岸常形成泥沙堆积。弯曲水流的速度分布和螺旋状次生流共同搬运泥沙，不能简单理解为水只向外侧直冲。随着外岸退后、内岸增长，弯道可能迁移；实际位置还取决于岸土黏性、植被根系、河流流量与人为护岸。

academic.title: 泥沙让水流留下证据
academic.body: 河流搬运的不只是水。较粗颗粒可能沿底部滚动、滑动或跳跃，细颗粒可悬浮在水中，溶解物则随水迁移。流速和水深改变搬运条件，但颗粒大小、密度与黏结也重要。比较不同时期的河岸线、沙洲和沉积层，可以寻找河道改变的证据；一次动画不能替代实际地形与流量测量。

zh.misconception: 河流拐弯不只是为了绕石头；外岸冲刷、内岸沉积是常见趋势，也有受地质和工程影响的例外。
zh.boundary: 河道形状是预设的教学示意，并未求解三维流体运动；流量、时间和泥沙浓度不能从画面读成实测值。

narration.label: 跟着水走
narration.text: 想象你站在安全的岸边，看一条小溪从山上流下来。它不是拿着尺子画直线，而是沿着地面能通过的地方往低处走。今天我们把小溪缩小到屏幕上。先看一眼前面的石头，猜猜水会从哪边绕过去，再慢慢往前推进。
narration.cue: 显示起点与石头，停三秒。

narration.label: 换一个条件
narration.text: 现在把石头换到另一边，再看一次。你发现河道的样子不一样了吗？这说明周围的地形会影响水的路线。不过，真正的大河拐弯还有很多原因。河岸软一点、硬一点，树根多一点、少一点，都可能让它经过很久以后变成不同的样子。
narration.cue: 切换石头位置，对照两条路径。

narration.label: 水带着小颗粒
narration.text: 找找河里的金色小点，它们代表泥沙。水一边流，一边搬着这些小颗粒。来到弯道时，两边受到的影响常常不一样：外侧的岸可能被冲走一些，内侧却可能堆起一些沙。先停一下，用手指分别指出外侧和内侧，不要只记住左边和右边。
narration.cue: 停在弯道，依次指向两岸。

narration.label: 慢慢改变的地图
narration.text: 河流在搬东西，也在慢慢改变自己的地图。一场洪水和许多年的流水，都可能留下痕迹。我们的小动画把长时间缩短了。下次和大人看河流时，可以从安全的地方找一找沙洲和弯道，想想哪些地方正在被搬走，哪些地方又收到了泥沙。
narration.cue: 留在最终全景，指出沙洲示意。

en.question: What happens when flowing water meets a rock? Do both sides of a bend change in the same way?
en.observe: Place the rock in the middle and advance water and sediment, then choose left or remove it. Compare the routes and the outer-bank erosion and inner-bank deposition markers.

academic.title: Water follows a hydraulic gradient
academic.body: Gravity, pressure differences and boundary resistance govern river flow. Water-surface elevation generally falls downstream, although local eddies can reverse the flow. Rocks, terrain and bed material influence routes. A bend need not start at one rock: small bank differences, floods and prolonged erosion also reshape channels.

academic.title: Bends connect erosion and deposition
academic.body: In many alluvial rivers, outer banks erode while inner banks accumulate sediment. Velocity differences and secondary circulation transport the grains. As the outer bank retreats and the inner bank grows, a bend can migrate. Cohesive soils, roots, discharge and engineered banks can alter this pattern.

academic.title: Sediment records river change
academic.body: Coarse grains can roll, slide or hop near the bed; finer material can remain suspended, and dissolved substances travel with the water. Transport depends on flow, grain size, density and cohesion. Comparing banks, bars and sediment layers over time provides evidence of change beyond a single simplified animation.

en.misconception: Rivers do not bend only to avoid rocks. Outer erosion and inner deposition are common patterns, with geological and engineered exceptions.
en.boundary: The channel is a preset teaching diagram, not a three-dimensional fluid simulation. Displayed motion does not measure discharge, time or sediment concentration.

narration.label: Follow the water
narration.text: Imagine watching a stream from a safe bank as it comes down a hill. It does not draw a ruler-straight line; it follows a route downhill through the landscape. Today the stream fits on our screen. Look at the rock ahead, predict which way water will pass, then move forward slowly.
narration.cue: Show the start and rock; pause for three seconds.

narration.label: Change one condition
narration.text: Move the rock to the other side and look again. Has the route changed? The landscape influences where water flows. Real rivers have many reasons to bend, though. Softer or harder banks, and more or fewer roots, can help the channel develop differently over a long time.
narration.cue: Switch the rock position and compare the routes.

narration.label: Water carries grains
narration.text: Find the gold dots representing sediment. Flowing water carries these little grains. At a bend, the two banks often change differently: some outer bank may wear away while sand gathers along the inside. Pause and point to the outside and inside of the bend, rather than memorizing left and right.
narration.cue: Pause at a bend and point to both banks.

narration.label: A changing map
narration.text: A river moves material and gradually redraws its own map. A flood and many years of flow can both leave traces. Our short animation compresses that long story. Next time you visit a river with an adult, look from a safe place for bars and bends, and wonder where sediment is leaving and arriving.
narration.cue: Hold the final overview and indicate the sediment bar.
